note: The scenarios offered for play on the table's new game screen (decision 0185). The screen reads nothing else of a scenario. For each, a game is offered only where a file makes it one: the engine's side given orders to its units ("script") or orders for its staff to carry out ("staff"), and a side played by a person or an agent given nothing. Each pairing names who holds each side (person, agent or engine) and the file. A rung of the ladder (decision 0237) is an invented game with no enemy: its other side is the engine's and has nothing ("engine": "absent"), it names no date for day 1, and its "mission" is the measure its verdict is read by. Each scenario names its map, key "map", a repository path, and the table draws the chart of that map (decision 0199); an entry with none is on the present map, data/map/south_pacific.csv, and every present entry names it. Kept by hand: a scenario renamed or moved is changed here. A file that names the ground figures is the copy in data/scenarios/table-hunger (for each battle that has submarines, the copy in data/scenarios/table-boats made from it by scripts/table-boats/make_files.py, decisions 0225 and 0227); for the 39 days, the copy in data/scenarios/table-rear-bases made from that by scripts/table-rear-bases/make_files.py, decision 0224's rulings of Nov 23, 2026 that names the figures of hunger that takes time (decision 0205, 3), made from the file on file by scripts/table-copies/make_copies.py; a file with no land units is the file on file. Listed simplest first: by its length and by how much a side has to run.

scenarios.name: Rung 1: One ship
lines: The first rung of the ladder: one ship, one order, no enemy.
You command at Base S, which has the stock, the fuel and the ship. Base T, 200 miles away, is the forward garrison.
A placeholder game: the sea, the bases, the ship and the men are invented.

sides.allied: Keep both garrisons fed. Every man, here and forward, is to be fed every night to the end of day 14. The forward garrison holds five days of food. Our own men eat from the stock you ship from, and it holds 5 t more than both need. Your one ship carries six days of the forward garrison's food at a time, and the fuel on hand is enough for two round trips.

scenarios.name: The Eastern Solomons
lines: One day of carrier battle. Two American carrier forces lie east of Guadalcanal; the Japanese carrier striking force and the Ryujo detachment come down from the north.

sides.allied: Find and sink the Japanese carriers supporting the reinforcement of Guadalcanal, and keep your own carriers in action.
sides.japanese: Destroy the American carriers east of Guadalcanal, and keep your own in action.

scenarios.name: The Coral Sea
lines: Two American carriers and a cruiser group meet two Japanese fleet carriers and a light carrier in the Coral Sea, while a Japanese convoy makes for Port Moresby with the men to take it.
Each side has an oiler with its carriers: the Neosho for the Allied side, the Toho Maru for the Japanese.
Each side has submarines at sea: one American boat off Cape St George, and three Japanese, one off Noumea and two off Port Moresby.

sides.allied: Stop the landing at Port Moresby and sink the Japanese carriers.
sides.japanese: Land the convoy's men at Port Moresby and sink the American carriers.

scenarios.name: Midway
lines: Three American carriers and the aircraft of Midway meet four Japanese fleet carriers, while a Japanese invasion force makes for the atoll with the men to take it.

Each side has its submarines on station: fourteen American boats on the arcs west and north-west of Midway, on a line to the east-north-east and far to the west, and one Japanese boat off the atoll itself.

sides.allied: Hold Midway and sink the Japanese carriers.
sides.japanese: Land the invasion force's men at Midway and sink the American carriers.

scenarios.name: The Eastern Solomons: five days
lines: The Eastern Solomons fought over five days. Two American carrier forces and the Marines at Lunga face a Japanese convoy bound for Guadalcanal, covered by the carrier striking force and the Ryujo detachment.
The Allied side has two oilers, the Platte and the Cimarron, at Efate. The Japanese side has none.
Submarines: one American boat due off Savo Island on the fourth day, and four Japanese, two north-east of Malaita, one coming east of it and one off Lunga.

sides.allied: Keep the airfield at Lunga open, stop the convoy, and sink the Japanese carriers while keeping your own.
sides.japanese: Land the convoy's men and supply on Guadalcanal, shut the airfield at Lunga, and sink the American carriers.

scenarios.name: Guadalcanal: the first thirty-nine days
lines: The landings on Guadalcanal and Tulagi and the weeks of fighting for the airfield at Lunga Point, at sea, in the air and ashore.

Submarines come on station through the weeks: five American boats, from Cape St George to Shortland and Savo Island, and eight Japanese, off Lunga and Tulagi, north-east of Malaita and south-east of San Cristobal.

sides.allied: Seize and hold Tulagi and the airfield at Lunga Point, to safeguard communications with Australia.
sides.japanese: Hold Lunga and Tulagi or take them back, close the airfield, sink what supplies it, and win the carrier fight.
